text:
Mateo: Heads-up — ap-southeast1c is seeing a big pile of tiny-gpu pods Pending since ~03:40 UTC. ~120 pending, a bunch of evictions observed but no single obvious taint/affinity reason. Anyone else noticing this?
Priya: Yep, saw the alert. Node telemetry shows NIC errors + higher conntrack drops on a subset of racks. Pods seem to consistently avoid nodes with label `network=restrictive` even though they meet resource requests. :thinking:
Alex: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/apac/gpu-pending — bandwidth on those racks is spiking and packet retries are up. CNI logs show repeated `ENETUNREACH` around the time pods try to bind.
Priya: I pulled scheduler traces. After the scoring change from the rollout earlier this week, nodes with `network=restrictive` are being penalized by the custom plugin for network saturation. snippet:
```
I0318 03:41:12.345 scheduler_pred: node/node-az3 network_score=-100 plugin=net-scorer reasons=[conntrack:high, tx-errors]
I0318 03:41:12.346 extenders: filtered out 7 candidates -> remaining 2
```
Mateo: So the scheduler is actively avoiding those nodes, which is fine, but that leaves a bunch of tiny-gpu pods that require co-located NVLINK/placement to fall through and end up Pending. Meanwhile reserved GPU pools are underutilized in the same AZ because they have `network=restrictive` label.
Linda: That explains the fragmentation pattern — we end up with many small pending pods that can't pack into the few nodes the scheduler prefers. Cost leak because reserved pools idle while on-demand is spinning up elsewhere.
DevEx: Any chance the scoring change accidentally interacts with the pod priority class? Could lower-priority tiny pods be getting pushed out/evicted when they do land?
Priya: Eviction logs show a mix: some pods evicted for `node.kubernetes.io/out-of-resource` and some force-evicted due to `network-unavailable` taint application during transient NIC flaps. Example: `kubectl describe pod` shows: `Warning  Evicted  kubelet  The node had condition: [NetworkUnavailable]`
Mateo: I created a quick grep of pending pod nodeAffinity to see why they don't land on reserved nodes — it's not affinity, it's the scheduler scoring.
Alex: Immediate mitigation: can we temporarily relax the net scorer weight to 0 for the tiny-gpu class? That should let the scheduler pick the reserved nodes and drain the Pending queue.
Linda: +1. We should also patch the reserved pool to add a `toleration` for `network=restrictive` taint until the NICs settle. Patch command to try (canary on two nodes first):
```
kubectl patch node node-az3-12 -p '{"spec":{"taints":[]}}' --type=merge
kubectl annotate node node-az3-12 rollme=canary
```
Priya: I'll revert the rollout weighting change in the scheduler policy for apac region and re-deploy a canary scheduler with the previous scores. Running `kubectl apply -f scheduler-policy-apac-canary.yaml` now.
SRE-bot: Incident INC-5678 created by Priya for ap-southeast1c GPU pending spike. Priority: P2. Assigned: @oncall-sre.
Mateo: I'll throttle new tiny-gpu job submissions from the batch queue to avoid amplifying the backlog.
DevEx: Can someone grab a prometheus query for conntrack drops and a list of nodes with `network=restrictive` label so we have before/after? I'll add it to the postmortem template.
Alex: Query I used: `sum(rate(conntrack_drops_total[5m])) by (instance)` and `kube_node_labels{label_network="restrictive"}`
Linda: Action items: 1) Priya revert net-scorer weight (canary done) 2) Patch tolerations on 2 reserved nodes (Mateo) 3) Throttle batch submissions (Mateo) 4) SRE runs NIC diagnostic script on impacted racks (assigned) 5) Postmortem w/ cost impact (DevEx)
Mateo: I'll run the patch canary now and post status in 10m.
Priya: Canary scheduler applied, initial traces show a drop in negative scoring for the reserved nodes. Watching Pending count.
SRE-bot: Update: INC-5678 status -> investigating.
Alex: Pending queue down from 120 -> 34 in 8m after canary/toleration patches. :thumbsup:
Mateo: Great. Keep monitoring for reappearance; we need a deeper follow-up to ensure scheduler-network interactions are explicit in the scoring docs.
DevEx: I'll draft a short runbook entry for this interaction (scheduler net-scorer + reserved-pool labels) and link the incident.
Priya: Filing a follow-up RFC to add tests for this scoring/label combo in our CI so future rollouts don't regress.
Linda: Thanks team — ping me if anything flips back. :eyes:
